correctness.rationale: Independence of the squares forces images of distinct natural basis vectors to have disjoint support, hence the change is monomial in any characteristic. The nonzero diagonal scales uniquely to 1, leaving only permutations. A nonzero ideal contains one basis square, then all three via full support; the argument survives every field extension. For D one can scale in the ambient entrywise-nonzero invertible family to unit diagonal. Distinct first-row/second-row ratio patterns distinguish a plane defined by an equation with two nonzero coefficients (q−1 squared torus solutions) from one with three (choose two nonzero inputs and exclude one ratio, giving (q−1)(q−2)). The fixed transposition factors as (1−x)(1+x−2yz), with x=−1 requiring special treatment in odd characteristic only. The circulant factor is a cube in characteristic 3; for q≡1 mod 3 the three torus lines have distinct pairwise intersections and no triple intersection, and for q≡2 mod 3 the two conjugate lines share only (1,1), not on the remaining line. For all-equal off-diagonals the excluded roots of (1−t)^2(1+2t) coalesce in characteristic 3; the second factor is constant in characteristic 2. Proper nontrivial stabilizer fixed sets intersect exactly on the S3-fixed locus, so subtraction and division by 6/h give the stated formulas. Independent exact orbit enumeration verified q=2,3,4,5,9; a separate seven-field stabilizer census also included q=7,8.
residual_risks: The finite reproductions corroborate the formulas but do not prove the all-prime-power statement. These are ordinary linear groups, not group schemes or semilinear automorphism groups.

originality.rationale: The all-prime-power four-stratum census is the supported distinct claim. Unit-diagonal permutation equivalence on the same full-support locus is already tabulated by Cabrera Casado–Siles Molina–Velasco under field restrictions. The S3 stratum alone, including its count, follows directly from Sriwongsa–Zou and is not a separate novelty. Their theorem and the overall Wei–Zou perfect-algebra census do not give the joint full-support distribution; computing the remaining locus-specific fixed counts is substantive.

value.rationale: At dimension three the natural permutation group first distinguishes involutions, three-cycles and full symmetry. Evaluating their multiplicities on the dense full-support family, including small fields and the characteristic-two and characteristic-three jumps, gives exact input for symmetry statistics that the ambient orbit total and the known S3-only classification cannot provide.
